summary: Pacific County DNR lookout: a 1942 wooden tower, a 1961 DNR replacement abandoned in 1967 and then removed or destroyed; old footings were photographed on private timber land.

facts.design: Wooden tower with a slant-walled 8x8 ft cab (1942); a DNR tower with an enclosed cab (1961)

access.note: Summit on private timber company land; WillhiteWeb says an access permit is required beyond the gates.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. Private timber land; ask the landowner before going past the gates.

facts.status_note: Tower abandoned in 1967 and gone; old concrete footings and a survey benchmark appear in WillhiteWeb's undated photos on private timber land.

events.note: Washington Division of Forestry tower with a slant-walled 8x8 ft cab; 30 ft per the register and FireLookout.com, 42 ft per WillhiteWeb and the 1953 survey
Replaced by a DNR tower: 50 ft per the register and FireLookout.com, 40 ft per WillhiteWeb
DNR biennial report for 1960 to 1962 says its crew built nine lookouts, one at Trap Creek
Maude Thompson is named as the lookout in 1964 and 1965 (WillhiteWeb's list repeats 1965)
Likely removed or destroyed shortly after 1967. The register says removed; FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed

corrections.why: No source gives 150 ft (45.7 m). The register and FireLookout.com give 50 ft (15.2 m) for the 1961 DNR tower; WillhiteWeb gives 40 ft, and the 1942 tower was 30 ft or 42 ft. Reviewer to choose which structure the record means.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1942 tower: 30 ft per the register and FireLookout.com, 42 ft per WillhiteWeb and the 1953 survey. 1961 DNR tower: 50 ft per the register and FireLookout.com, 40 ft per WillhiteWeb. The story gives no single height.
The register says the tower was likely removed after 1967; FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The record's 'gone' fits both.
A 1967 survey note says the tower had been torn down and rebuilt south of the mark. That may describe the 1961 replacement, but the note gives no date.

notes_for_editor: Heights disagree across all four sources; the brief's 45.7 m (150 ft) matches none, see corrections. Removal versus destruction is worded differently but not contradicted. Staffing comes from one source (WillhiteWeb) that repeats the year 1965. Access and the site today rest on WillhiteWeb's undated text and captions, which mention 2015; no source from 2026 was found. One web search returned nothing on this lookout.
